# PatternSection

PatternSection: a span of the page grid under one heading, with its header, toolbar and tabs.

Also asked as: page section, toolbar, section header, block, region.

## Usage

Use `PatternSection` when content has a heading, shares actions, shows or hides as a unit, or takes its own span of the grid; otherwise the content belongs to the Section above it. The header is the Section's, not the Table's: the title row names it, and the view bar under it holds the views at the start and everything that acts on the content at the end, so switching views can swap a table for cards while the bar stays put.

A Section has two looks, `none` and `subtle`, and five parts: header, body, side, detail and footer. The side takes either fill; the detail is an inline expand on the subtle fill that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down.

## Motion

PatternSection reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| view-bar | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Title row: nothing moves. The selected pill's fill and the format switch's indicator glide while the content swaps in place. Search and the Filter count grow to the left. |
| side-open | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The side opens and collapses as a section. Below 960 it hides with no animation. |
| side-close | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Collapses back the same way. Below 960 the side is gone in the same frame, with no animation. |
| detail | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. |
| body | Load content | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Content loads on arrival; add or remove, reorder and swap content as it changes. |
| footer | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Paging is Step. |

## Alternatives

- For one object with an agreed shape, use `PatternCard` inside a Section.
- For a queue page or a quick look at a row from a table, use `Panel`.
- For the page's own title, use `PageHeader`; a Section stands under it.

## Best practices

### Make a Section only when it earns one. {#make-a-section-only-when-it-earns-one}

**Checked:** Review

A Section earns its own heading, its own actions or its own place in the grid. When its heading would repeat its only card's title, drop the Section and let the card stand on its own.

Do: A card with its own title stands on its own in the page.
Don't: A Section whose heading repeats its only card's title: two headings for one thing.

### Put the title row first and the view bar under it. {#put-the-title-row-first-and-the-view-bar-under-it}

**Checked:** Automatic

The title row sits `--section-stack-sm` above the view bar, and the header sits `--section-stack-md` above the body. The title, the first pill's label and the first column's text share one left edge. At every width the two stay separate rows: below the narrow width the description truncates first, then Search collapses, the format switch shows icons, extra pills fold and the Primary keeps only its icon.

Do: The title row first, the view bar under it, sharing one left edge.
Don't: The title pushed into the view bar: the heading and the pills fight for the start, and the description has nowhere to go.

### Put actions in the title row only when there is no view bar. {#put-actions-in-the-title-row-only-when-there-is-no-view-bar}

**Checked:** Review

Each action has one home. With a view bar, every action sits at its end.

Do: No view bar, so the actions sit at the end of the title row.
Don't: Actions in the title row and again in the view bar: one action, two homes.

### Keep views at the start as pills that hug their labels. {#keep-views-at-the-start-as-pills-that-hug-their-labels}

**Checked:** Review

Views are a fixed set the product defines, and one pill stays even with one view. The strip stays on one line; extra pills fold into More. Under page tabs, the views become one labeled PopupSelect, so the page keeps one tab system.

### Order the end of the bar: format switch, Search, filters, More, Primary. {#order-the-end-of-the-bar-format-switch-search-filters-more-primary}

**Checked:** Review

Filter and More are icon buttons with Tooltips; Search is a compact `SearchField` (`spacing="compact"`, and `isCollapsible` where the bar is tight); the Primary is labeled and last. Keep five controls at most and fold extras into More. Search, Filter and the Primary stay in the bar. Every control is a default button, or compact in a compact bar.

Do: Format switch, Search, Filter, More, then the labeled Primary last.
Don't: Six controls in no order, the Primary first and a second labeled button: fold extras into More.

### Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected. {#turn-the-head-row-into-the-bulk-bar-when-rows-are-selected}

**Checked:** Automatic

The part-ticked select-all, the count of selected rows, then the actions, all at the start. The checkboxes clear the selection, so the bar carries no Cancel. Selected rows take the selected fill and the view bar stays put. Only the Dynamic table selects rows.

### Drop the Filter icon while a filter side shows. {#drop-the-filter-icon-while-a-filter-side-shows}

**Checked:** Review

Each control has one home. The icon returns with its count once the side hides, below `SECTION_DETAIL_FLOOR`.

### Use a Section detail as an inline expand, never on a queue page. {#use-a-section-detail-as-an-inline-expand-never-on-a-queue-page}

**Checked:** Review

A **Section detail** is an inline expand: a row or card opens in place inside its Section and pushes the content below it down. It is never the detail view on a queue page — a queue page docks a `Panel` beside the list instead, and the record opens on demand.

### Keep the footer for paging and "View all". {#keep-the-footer-for-paging-and-view-all}

**Checked:** Review

Actions that commit changes belong in the card or form that holds the fields.

Do: The form card holds its own Save; the Section footer is for paging and "View all".
Don't: Cancel and Save in the Section footer, away from the fields they commit.

### Use the subtle fill only to stand apart. {#use-the-subtle-fill-only-to-stand-apart}

**Checked:** Review

The subtle fill sets a part apart from its neighbor, such as a detail or a filter side. Plain Sections take no fill.

### Nest a Section once at most. {#nest-a-section-once-at-most}

**Checked:** Review

A subsection is an h3. A Section that already has a view bar holds subsections without one.

The table's empty state replaces the whole table, by the Empty pattern; elevation and fills follow Elevation.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading whose level follows nesting: h2 for a Section, h3 for a subsection. With the view bar alone the title stays in the page, hidden from sight.
- The pill views are a tablist; the selected tab says which rows the body shows. Views swap in place.
- Search, Filter and More carry their names: "Search students", "Filters, 2 applied", "More". The Filter count is in the name as well as on the button.
- The table announces a selection politely, "2 selected", and the bulk bar's actions follow the select-all checkbox in the tab order.
- The detail is a collapsible region named by its title: the disclosure button toggles it with Enter or Space, and Escape inside the open detail closes it and returns focus to the button.

## Types

Each Section type combines a header and body, with an optional side or detail. These are starting layouts of the same component.

- **List.** The view bar alone, one table, paging. The default for an area page.
- **Detail.** A list with a detail that opens an item in place.
- **Cards.** Title and actions, a grid of cards three across.
- **Stats.** A row of cards, each one number and its label, four at most.
- **Details.** Label and value pairs in two columns, with Edit in the title row.
- **Main and side.** A split with the side at the end and no fill: facts beside the main content.
- **Form.** Fields in a card, with the card's own Save and Cancel at its bottom.
- **Subsections.** Sections nested one level, each an h3, for a long settings page.

## Header types

A starting set, picked by what the Section holds. Every control state lives on its component: Icon button, Filter button and Tabs. Which filters the bar takes is Filtering; how the search field behaves is the Search pattern, listed in Patterns.

- **Title.** A title and a description, nothing to act on. Most Sections that hold cards or a form.
- **Title and actions.** Section actions in the title row. One Primary and two others at most.
- **View bar, one view.** One pill names the rows and stays, so nothing moves when a second view arrives.
- **View bar, several views.** Two to five views of the same rows, a fixed set the product defines. Extra pills fold into More.
- **Format switch.** When the rows show as a table or cards, equal-width segments sit first at the end.
- **View bar alone.** The page title already names the collection, so the title row is hidden from sight and stays in the page for screen readers.
- **Under page tabs.** One tab system per page: the views become one labeled PopupSelect at the start of the bar. It picks a view, not a filter.
- **Subsection.** Any type nests once. The title drops to an h3; the view bar keeps its size.

## Anatomy

A Section with a view bar, a detail and a footer. The title, the first pill and the first column share one left edge.

1. **Title row.** The h2, an optional one-line description, and actions only when there is no view bar.
2. **View bar** (optional). Pill views at the start; at the end, in order, the format switch, Search, filters, More and the labeled Primary.
3. **Body.** A Table, a card grid, a list, a form or subsections. A Table's head row follows the bar with nothing between.
4. **Detail** (optional). An inline expand on the subtle fill that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. Never use it for a queue page, which docks a `Panel` beside the list.
5. **Footer** (optional). Paging or "View all".

## Slots

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` · `description` · `actions` | The title row. |
| `viewBar` | Planned. Pill Tabs at the start; at the end the format switch, Search, the filters, More and the labeled Primary. Today the view bar goes in `tabs`. |
| `toolbar` | A `SectionToolbar`, the row under the title row for the search, filters and actions of a table. Pass a `PatternSection.Toolbar` as the `toolbar` prop. It takes the place of `tabs` when both are passed. |
| `tabs` · `type="tabs-only"` | The row under the title row; `tabs-only` hides the title row from sight when the page title names the collection. |
| `fill` | `none` or `subtle`, for the Section; the detail always takes `subtle`. |
| `children` | The body: a Table, a card grid, a list, a form or subsections. |
| `layout="split"` · `side` | A second column at the end, for a summary. |
| `sidePlacement` | Planned. `start` puts the side first, for a filter side or a step rail. |
| `detail` · `detailTitle` · `detailDescription` · `detailFooter` | An inline expand that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. Never use it for a queue page, which docks a `Panel`. |
| `detailOpen` · `defaultDetailOpen` · `onDetailOpenChange` | Open state of the inline detail expand. |
| `footer` | Paging or "View all". |

The bulk bar lives in the Dynamic table's head row, through its `bulkActions`, and the Section holds nothing for it: Dynamic table.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the Section with what it holds, in sentence case: "Upcoming sessions". | A title that repeats the only card inside it. |
| Keep the description to one line: "Lincoln Middle · 24 students". | A paragraph under the title. |
| Name views by the rows they show: "All students", "Needs follow-up". | Views of different things in one strip. |
| Name the scope in Search: "Search students". | A bare "Search". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `title` | node | — | Section title: an h2 at Heading/medium 20, or an h3 at Heading/small 16 inside another section |
| `description` | node | — | Optional description under the title, Body/default |
| `actions` | node | — | Actions slot, aligned to the end of the title row |
| `tabs` | node | — | Tabs row under the title row (header type `tabs`, or `tabs-only`) |
| `toolbar` | node | — | Toolbar row under the title row (header type `toolbar`), usually a `PatternSection.Toolbar` |
| `header` | node | — | Free-form header in place of title and description (header type `custom`) |
| `type` | enum | — | Header type. Read from the slots when left off; pass `tabs-only` to show only the tabs row |
| `onAddView` | func | — | Puts "Add view" at the end of the tabs row, and runs when it is pressed |
| `addViewLabel` | string | `'Add view'` | The "Add view" button's label |
| `loading` | bool | `false` | Swaps the header for skeleton bars and marks the section busy |
| `layout` | enum | `'single'` | Body layout: the content alone, content beside `side`, or stacked subsections |
| `side` | node | — | Side column of `layout="split"` |
| `footer` | node | — | Footer, for "View all" or paging only; aligned to the end |
| `detail` | node | — | Inline expand content that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down |
| `detailTitle` | node | — | Title on the detail disclosure button; also names the detail region |
| `detailDescription` | node | — | Optional description on the detail disclosure button |
| `detailFooter` | node | — | Detail footer, such as "Open full review" |
| `detailOpen` | bool | — | Controlled open state of the inline detail expand |
| `defaultDetailOpen` | bool | `false` | Whether an uncontrolled inline detail expand starts open |
| `onDetailOpenChange` | func | — | Called with the next open boolean when the inline detail expand toggles |
| `level` | enum | — | `page` makes the title the page's h1 at Heading/large 24; by default it nests one level down |
| `gap` | enum | `'md'` | Gap between the header, the body and the footer (Section/stack tokens); `md` is the Figma value |
| `fill` | enum | `'none'` | `subtle` sets the section on the sunken surface with a pad and a radius; `none` (default) draws nothing |
| `named` | bool | `false` | Makes the section a region named by its title, for a section that stands apart as a landmark |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |
| `children` | node | — | Content slot; with `layout="split"`, the main column |
